Subject: Request for pen test report and remediation details

Jordan —

Following the public incident at a vendor in our supply chain last week, our compliance team has asked for the latest penetration test report and a current remediation status for any critical/high findings. We need the documentation to complete an elevated risk review for our board.

Specifically, could you provide:
- Latest pen test report (redacted if needed)
- Remediation matrix / status for critical & high items
- Any relevant SOC 2 or SIG evidence related to testing cadence

Please let me know what you can share and what the process is. If there are forms or NDAs we need to complete, point me to them and we’ll prioritize. Target for our internal review is end of week (EOW).

Thanks,
Ryan Chen
Head of InfoSec — MediSafe Health
security@medisafe.com

Subject: Re: Request for pen test report and remediation details

Ryan —

Thanks for the note and the heads-up on the board review. We can support this, but we do have a standard process for sharing penetration testing artifacts: a redacted executive summary and a remediation matrix are usually shared directly; the full raw report is provided only after an NDA and a short justification (and then on a time-limited secure link).

To move quickly:
1) Can you confirm the recipient(s) who need access (names + emails)?
2) Will MediSafe require the unredacted report or will a fully redacted exec summary + remediation matrix suffice for your board?
3) If you need the full report, we’ll send a DocuSign NDA and ask you to return it; once signed we can provision a restricted download link.

Looping in Evelyn from Security to outline redaction policy and an ETA. I’ll pull the necessary documents once we have the recipients and scope.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hi Ryan / Jordan —

Quick note from Security on our sharing policy and timelines so expectations are clear:

What we can share immediately (within 48 hours):
- Redacted executive summary (removes IP/third-party toolchains and internal findings that could facilitate attacks)
- A remediation matrix summarizing severity, status, and expected close dates for any critical/high findings

What requires additional controls (full report):
- Full, unredacted penetration test reports contain exploit details and are treated as highly restricted. We require:
  * A signed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) or Mutual Risk Agreement (MRA) that includes restricted handling language; and
  * A named list of recipients (security resp. roles only) and justification for needing the full contents.

Once the NDA/MRA is executed we can provision an ephemeral, access-logged S3 link (seven-day expiry) to the full report. Typical timeline for full-report access after NDA is 3–7 business days (depends on redaction review and legal sign-off).

I’m attaching our redaction guidance and I’ll prepare the executive summary and remediation matrix for you once Jordan confirms recipients.

Attachments: [redaction_guidance.pdf]

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
